a39b75c013f25931d216d70e7c49d107cae90b46.summary: Project page for Sliver, an open-source, cross-platform adversary emulation and red team framework intended for authorised security testing. It describes command-and-control over mTLS, WireGuard, HTTP(S) and DNS, support for macOS, Windows and Linux, and GPLv3 licensing with install instructions. It describes a tool, not a threat actor, campaign, malware incident or vulnerability, so it is not a threat report.

a35cc21a595cd3651df0e7ad8e3f2eb726939764.summary: GitHub repository README by Tillmann Werner about the Conficker computer worm. It provides YARA rules to detect unpacked worm variants in memory, Snort rules to detect exploitation attempts in a network, and unpacked sample versions of each Conficker generation, which the README warns contain malicious code. The last commit is dated November 20, 2018, and the data is stated as copyright 2008-2018.

a32666781a0f2225f289f72a0537cc3b6a031ad9.summary: Elastic Security Labs describes REF5961, a state-aligned intrusion set targeting government bodies in Southern and Southeastern Asia, including a foreign affairs ministry of an ASEAN member and Mongolian government-related infrastructure. The report discloses three malware families (EAGERBEE, RUDEBIRD, DOWNTOWN) and a BLOODALCHEMY backdoor added in an October 2023 update. It links the activity to the REF2924 intrusion set and to a China-nexus actor, stating varying degrees of confidence. Shared C2 hosting, code overlap and co-residence support the associations, and several attributions are…

hedges: China-nexus attribution rests on correlated execution flows, tooling, infrastructure and victimology plus third-party reports; the report calls it confidence, not certainty.
DOWNTOWN is attributed with a moderate degree of confidence to a nationally sponsored Chinese threat actor.
The report cannot confirm that the self-signed certificate infrastructure was used for EAGERBEE or RUDEBIRD.
It is unclear whether PsExec was brought in by the threat actor or was already present in the environment.
It is not clear how the Mongolian infrastructure was compromised or the extent to which it has been used.
The report speculates that multiple players in the REF2924 organization may have been active in the environment.
Same tasking authority is stated with a high degree of confidence, based on shared hosting and service-availability coordination.
The report did not find network or communication functionality, or any domain or IP tied to the DOWNTOWN sample.
